newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Friday with investors continuing to liquidate their positions in the March contract ahead of the delivery date, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,330 yuan ($401) per tonne, losing two yuan. It opened at 2,226 and hit a low of 2,225 yuan per tonne.
March fell seven to 3,130, May did not trade, July rose 45 to 3,415, November fell two to 3,340 and January 1998 contract put on two to 3,350.
Combined volume fell to 36,600 tonnes from 47,900.
"Most investors were eager to liquidate their positions in the March contract because most of them do not want physical goods," one trader said. The March contract expires next Tuesday.
"There were also many investors staying on the sidelines with market trend unclear," he added.
The Shanghai Cereals & Oils Exchange said on Friday that it would cancel the trade commission on soybean contracts for a month from next Monday.
Traders said the measures would make soybeans active in the next few days. ($1=8.2956 yuan)
